daily.brief: 過去約30小時只有41則帖、21個帳號在聊，氣氛偏淡。共同看淡落在指數：@RedDogT3 指出 $QQQ 快速跌破680調整、$SPY 跌破762缺口樞紐改變局勢；高盛交易臺也說防衛跡象有限。分歧在 $NVDA，一邊 @Beth_Kindig 講Vera Rubin NVL72機架明年總價值可超3倍至7110億，另一邊 @howardlindzon 提到科技股單日價值毀滅2.5萬億（半個NVDA）只是小傷。最大變化是MSFT據報逐步減少向 $ORCL 租用舊NVDA容量、轉新GPU，讓AI基建供應鏈重新分配變得具體。
daily.full:
共識

共同看好幾乎空白，只有 $APP 有兩則看好：@Mr_Derivatives 問「什麼股市崩盤？！」因為過去5天 $APP +72%、$U +41%；@michaelsikand 提到有人在底部公開買入後出現50%反轉。共同看淡比較清楚，集中在大盤技術位。

共同看淡

@RedDogT3 直接說 $QQQ 快速跌破680以調整（原帖），$SPY 也跌破762缺口樞紐改變局勢（原帖）。@carlquintanilla 轉高盛交易臺：任何地方防衛跡象有限，市場仍然非常艱難，$NDX 正在重新測試過去幾年基礎趨勢線。@howardlindzon 把科技股有史以來最糟糕單日價值毀滅2.5萬億（半個 $NVDA）形容成小傷、退化經濟警鐘，並引述「如果你必須恐慌就早點恐慌」像今年6月。$ORCL 也有兩則看淡，都跟MSFT減租舊容量有關。

分歧

@Beth_Kindig 看好 $NVDA，因為機架複雜度上升讓OEM每部署能捕獲更多價值，Vera Rubin NVL72預計明年總機架輸出價值提升超過3倍至7110億美元（原帖）。但 @howardlindzon 把同一天的大跌看成更深層問題，@StockSavvyShay 則中性解釋MSFT減少從 $ORCL 租舊 $NVDA 容量、審視數十億雲端交易，更像轉向更新GPU而非退出AI支出，還提到MSFT要求 $IREN 升級GB300（原帖）。@ripster47 直接說這是 $ORCL 利空、拋售 $SOXL。

其他值得留意

@SJosephBurns 強調這個市場關鍵技術水平非常重要，明天會出每日/每週圖表水平，涵蓋 $SPY $QQQ $IWM $AMD $NVDA 等。@Mr_Derivatives 統計下週五13日星期五過去11次 $QQQ 有8次上漲，不過這是中性觀察。整體討論量低，沒有太多新目標價出現。

短摘要

41帖、21帳號的安靜一日。指數技術位被跌破成共同看淡焦點，$NVDA 則因機架價值預期與大盤毀滅數字出現分歧，MSFT減租 $ORCL 舊容量讓供應鏈調整變具體。

weekly.brief: 過去7日672則帖、91個帳號，共同看好14隻、看淡4隻、分歧27隻。最明顯的共識是財報後的個股：$AAPL 有4個帳號看好（超預期、指引優於預期、短期弱但大趨勢穩），$COHR、$AEHR 也因業績與產能預訂受追捧。共同看淡集中在 $CRWV、$ASTS 等。分歧最激烈的是 $INTC（3多6空）、$ORCL（1多7空，Stephens升至超配目標213但MSFT減租消息壓制）、$SPY/$QQQ 則多空接近。最大變化是光學與測試設備在AI基建熱潮中重新被定價，而大盤情緒仍在技術位與輪動之間拉鋸。
weekly.full:
共識

$AAPL 是本週最乾淨的共同看好之一。@TrendSpider 報道第四季盈收雙超：EPS 2.10對預期1.98、營收1144.77億對1133.92億。@munster_gene 說投資者錯過更大重點：12月收入指引優於華爾街預期，比略軟利潤率指引重要。@MarkNewtonCMT 承認短期動能不穩、過去一個月給短線交易者警告，但較大趨勢穩健無明顯惡化，本週弱勢可能短暫。$COHR 也有3個看好：@michaelsikand 指光子學逆向交易，CEO說需求無減弱、2027基本上已預訂滿、客戶訂到2028。@StockSavvyShay 與 @aleabitoreddit 都提到Marvell光學併購後 $COHR 遭賣壓，但產能已售至2029、戰略價值上升。$AEHR 同樣有3個帳號因財報強勁（EPS 0.28對0.11、營收3300萬對2700萬、上調展望）看好。

共同看淡

$CRWV 有3個帳號看淡、0個看好。$ASTS 也是3看淡。$BE 與 $CBRS 各有2個看淡。這些多集中在AI基建相關但估值或執行受質疑的名字上，與本週大盤技術壓力互相呼應。

分歧

$INTC 最分裂：3個看好、6個看淡。$ORCL 則是1多7空，但 @WallStJesus 轉 Stephens 從平等權重升至超配、目標價從185上調至213美元；同一時間 @StockSavvyShay 與 @ripster47 都在講MSFT逐步減少向甲骨文租用舊NVDA容量、審視數十億雲端交易。$SPY 有3多4空、討論68帖：@michaelsikand 認為是AI恐懼高峯、資本支出數字不變、資金輪動到價值後很快會FOMO回場；@RyanDetrick 指正離開歷史最差六個月、接下來六個月是標普500最好時期；@Stephanie_Link 則用10月數據（下跌93bp但9個板塊上漲、突破50日線股票從20%升至61%、主經紀商最大減倉）看年底設置。$QQQ 同樣多空接近。$NVDA 4多3空，延續每日的機架價值與大盤毀滅對比。$TSLA 與 $AMZN 則多頭佔優（各7多1空）。

其他值得留意

$LLY、$SKHY、$APP、$TEM、$CRWD 都有2個共同看好，顯示非純半導體的主題也在動。整體討論量大增到672帖，但共同看淡只有4隻，分歧遠多於單邊共識，反映市場在財報季與技術位之間仍在找方向。

monthly.brief: 過去28日6539則帖、154個帳號，共同看好67隻、看淡19隻、分歧129隻。最穩的共識是 $SOFI（9個看好、0看淡）、$RSP、$MA、$LLY、$COHR 等。共同看淡最突出的是 $RDDT（9看淡，8個交易日跌42%、AI擾亂搜索）。分歧最深的是大盤 $SPY（16多15空、577帖）與 $CRWV（3多25空）。最大變化是AI基建相關個股與傳統權重股同時被重新定價，而指數本身仍在多空拉鋸中。
monthly.full:
共識

$SOFI 是本月最乾淨的共同看好，9個帳號、0看淡。@Jake__Wujastyk 說它是少數月線蠟燭收盤看起來不錯的之一；@OptionsMike 認為財報很好、大幅回落後容易反彈、需站上200日線；@RedDogT3 指近期少見像昨日財報後這樣的形態，策略以跳空缺口樞紐做多波段。$RSP 有6個看好、$MA 也有6個。$LLY 5個看好，@APompliano 引 Jordi Visser 認為禮來將成全球最有價值公司，受惠醫療支出加大量AI投資，而 $NVDA 更易受顛覆。$COHR 同樣5個看好，延續週線的產能與併購邏輯。$AMD 有4個看好但討論量高達160帖，顯示關注度極高。

共同看淡

$RDDT 最集中：9個看淡、0看好、47帖。@KobeissiLetter 指與Reddit CEO業績電話會議將被引用多年，8個交易日內下跌42%，AI已經永遠擾亂搜索以及更廣泛互聯網。@kevinxu 也說自己早講過會大幅錯過。$BA 有4個看淡，$FTNT、$RBLX、$HYG 各有3個。

分歧

$SPY 是討論量之王，577帖、16多15空，幾乎完全分裂。$CRWV 則是3多25空、239帖，看淡佔絕對優勢，但 @APompliano 引 Dan Ives 解釋為何AI看淡者錯誤（債務相對訂單積壓微不足道、每1美元資本開支有5-6倍乘數、華爾街低估未來12個月），@OptionsHawk 也提到有人大手押注2027年3月85美元認購。$TSLA 22多3空、$SPCX 18多5空，多頭明顯。$MU 12多9空、$QQQ 9多10空、$META 14多5空、$INTC 5多14空，各有自己的多空理由。整體分歧數量遠超共同共識，顯示28日內市場在不同主題間快速輪動。

其他值得留意

共同看好名單很長（67隻），涵蓋金融、醫療、能源、半導體設備等多個方向，不像單一日或一週那麼集中。$XOM、$CVX、$ISRG、$UNH 都有穩定看好帳號。討論總量6539帖說明這段時間資訊密度很高，但單邊共識只集中在少數名字上。

briefing.html:
今日簡報

過去約30小時討論量偏低（41帖），但方向清楚：指數技術位被跌破成共同看淡焦點，@RedDogT3 點名 $QQQ 680與 $SPY 762。$NVDA 出現分歧，一邊有Vera Rubin機架明年價值大增至7110億的預期，另一邊有科技股單日毀滅2.5萬億的敘事。最具體的變化是MSFT據報減少向 $ORCL 租用舊 $NVDA 容量、轉更新GPU，讓AI基建供應鏈重新分配不再只是抽象話題。7日與28日視角則顯示財報個股（$AAPL、$COHR、$AEHR、$SOFI）有較乾淨共識，而大盤與部分AI基建名字仍高度分裂。

daily.brief: Only 41 posts from 21 accounts in the last ~30 hours, and the tone leans cautious. Common bearish views sit on the indices: @RedDogT3 notes $QQQ quickly broke below 680 for a pullback and $SPY broke the 762 gap pivot, changing the setup; Goldman’s trading desk also sees limited defensive signs. Divergence appears on $NVDA, with @Beth_Kindig highlighting Vera Rubin NVL72 racks potentially more than tripling total rack output value to $711B next year, while @howardlindzon frames the $2.5T single-day tech value destruction (half of NVDA) as just a flesh wound. The clearest shift is the report that MSFT is gradually reducing older NVDA capacity leased from $ORCL and shifting toward newer GPUs, making AI infrastructure reallocation concrete.
daily.full:
Consensus

Common bullish views are almost empty. Only $APP has two: @Mr_Derivatives asks “what market crash?!” after $APP +72% and $U +41% over five days from trough to peak; @michaelsikand notes someone publicly bought the bottom and then saw a 50% reversal. Common bearish views are clearer and centered on index technical levels.

Common Bearish

@RedDogT3 directly says $QQQ quickly broke below 680 for a pullback (post) and $SPY broke the 762 gap pivot, changing the setup (post). @carlquintanilla relays Goldman’s desk: limited defensive signs anywhere, the market remains very tough, and $NDX is retesting the base trendline of recent years. @howardlindzon describes the worst single-day tech value destruction ever ($2.5T, half an $NVDA) as a flesh wound and a warning for a degenerate economy, quoting “if you have to panic, panic early” like June this year. $ORCL also has two bearish posts tied to the MSFT capacity news.

Divergence

@Beth_Kindig is bullish on $NVDA because rising rack complexity lets server OEMs capture more value per deployment; Vera Rubin NVL72 is expected to lift total rack output value more than 3x to $711B next year (post). @howardlindzon treats the same day’s drop as a deeper issue. @StockSavvyShay is more neutral, explaining that MSFT reducing older $NVDA capacity from $ORCL and reviewing tens of billions in cloud deals looks more like a shift to newer GPUs than an exit from AI spending, and notes MSFT asking $IREN to upgrade GB300 (post). @ripster47 calls it negative for $ORCL and sells $SOXL.

Other Notes

@SJosephBurns stresses that key technical levels matter a lot in this market and will publish daily/weekly chart levels tomorrow covering $SPY $QQQ $IWM $AMD $NVDA etc. @Mr_Derivatives notes that of the past 11 Friday the 13ths, $QQQ rose in 8 of them, though this is a neutral observation. Overall volume is low and few new price targets appeared.

weekly.brief: Over 7 days: 672 posts, 91 accounts, 14 common-bullish names, 4 common-bearish, 27 split. Cleanest consensus is post-earnings: $AAPL has 4 accounts bullish (beat, better December guidance, short-term weak but larger trend intact); $COHR and $AEHR also draw support on results and booked capacity. Common bearish views cluster on $CRWV, $ASTS and similar. Sharpest splits are $INTC (3 bull / 6 bear), $ORCL (1 / 7, Stephens upgrade to Overweight with $213 target vs MSFT capacity reduction), and $SPY/$QQQ near even. Biggest change is optical and test equipment being re-priced inside the AI infrastructure wave while index sentiment still tugs between technical levels and rotation.
weekly.full:
Consensus

$AAPL is one of the cleanest common-bullish names this week. @TrendSpider reports Q4 beat: EPS $2.10 vs $1.98 expected, revenue $114.477B vs $113.392B. @munster_gene says investors missed the bigger point: December revenue guidance better than Wall Street expected matters more than the slightly softer margin guide. @MarkNewtonCMT admits short-term momentum is shaky and the past month warned short-term traders, but the larger trend remains solid with no clear deterioration, so this week’s weakness may be temporary. $COHR has 3 bullish accounts: @michaelsikand calls photonics a ready-made reverse trade; CEO says no signs of demand weakening, 2027 essentially booked out, customers booking into 2028. @StockSavvyShay and @aleabitoreddit both note selling pressure on $COHR after the Marvell optics deal but point to capacity already sold through 2029 and rising strategic value. $AEHR likewise has 3 accounts bullish on a strong print (EPS $0.28 vs $0.11, revenue $33M vs $27M, raised outlook).

Common Bearish

$CRWV has 3 bearish accounts and zero bullish. $ASTS also has 3 bearish. $BE and $CBRS each have 2. These sit mainly on AI-infrastructure names whose valuation or execution is being questioned, echoing the week’s index technical pressure.

Divergence

$INTC is the most split: 3 bullish, 6 bearish. $ORCL is 1 bull / 7 bear, yet @WallStJesus relays Stephens raising it from Equal-Weight to Overweight and lifting the target from $185 to $213; at the same time @StockSavvyShay and @ripster47 are discussing MSFT gradually reducing older NVDA capacity leased from Oracle and reviewing tens of billions in cloud deals. $SPY has 3 bull / 4 bear across 68 posts: @michaelsikand sees an AI fear peak, unchanged capex numbers, rotation into value, and expects FOMO back soon; @RyanDetrick notes we are leaving the historically worst six months and the next six are the best for the S&P 500; @Stephanie_Link uses October stats (down 93 bp but 9 of 11 sectors up, stocks above 50-day rising from 20% to 61%, largest prime-brokerage de-risking) to frame the year-end setup. $QQQ is similarly balanced. $NVDA is 4 / 3, continuing the rack-value versus market-destruction contrast. $TSLA and $AMZN lean bullish (7 / 1 each).

Other Notes

$LLY, $SKHY, $APP, $TEM and $CRWD each have 2 common-bullish accounts, showing non-pure-semiconductor themes also moving. Discussion volume jumped to 672 posts, but only 4 common-bearish names exist; splits far outnumber one-sided consensus, reflecting a market still searching for direction between earnings and technical levels.

monthly.brief: Over 28 days: 6,539 posts, 154 accounts, 67 common-bullish, 19 common-bearish, 129 split. Steadiest consensus is $SOFI (9 bullish, 0 bearish), followed by $RSP, $MA, $LLY, $COHR. Sharpest common-bearish is $RDDT (9 bearish, down 42% in 8 trading days, AI disrupting search). Deepest splits are the broad market $SPY (16 bull / 15 bear, 577 posts) and $CRWV (3 / 25). Biggest change is simultaneous re-pricing of AI-infrastructure names and traditional large-caps while the indices themselves remain in a tug-of-war.
monthly.full:
Consensus

$SOFI is the cleanest common-bullish name of the month: 9 accounts, zero bearish. @Jake__Wujastyk says it is one of the few monthly candles that closed looking decent; @OptionsMike notes the earnings were good, it is easy to bounce after a sharp pullback, and it needs to reclaim the 200-day; @RedDogT3 points out how rare a post-earnings shape like yesterday’s has been and describes a strategy of using the gap-pivot for swing longs. $RSP has 6 bullish accounts, $MA also has 6. $LLY has 5; @APompliano cites Jordi Visser arguing Lilly could become the world’s most valuable company, benefiting from ongoing healthcare spending plus heavy AI investment, while $NVDA is more vulnerable to disruption. $COHR likewise has 5 bullish accounts, continuing the capacity and deal logic from the weekly view. $AMD has 4 bullish but 160 posts, showing extremely high attention.

Common Bearish

$RDDT is the most concentrated: 9 bearish, 0 bullish, 47 posts. @KobeissiLetter says the earnings call with Reddit’s CEO will be cited for years; the stock fell 42% in 8 trading days and AI has permanently disrupted search and the broader internet. @kevinxu also notes he said it would miss big. $BA has 4 bearish; $FTNT, $RBLX and $HYG each have 3.

Divergence

$SPY is the discussion-volume king: 577 posts, 16 bull / 15 bear, almost perfectly split. $CRWV is 3 bull / 25 bear across 239 posts, with bears dominant, yet @APompliano cites Dan Ives explaining why AI bears are wrong (debt tiny relative to backlog, every $1 of capex has a 5-6x multiplier, Wall Street underestimates the next 12 months) and @OptionsHawk notes large bullish bets on the March 2027 85 calls. $TSLA is 22 / 3 and $SPCX 18 / 5, clearly bullish. $MU is 12 / 9, $QQQ 9 / 10, $META 14 / 5, $INTC 5 / 14, each with their own reasons. Overall the number of splits far exceeds one-sided consensus, showing rapid theme rotation across the 28 days.

Other Notes

The common-bullish list is long (67 names) and spans financials, healthcare, energy, semiconductor equipment and more; it is far less concentrated than the daily or weekly views. $XOM, $CVX, $ISRG and $UNH all have steady bullish accounts. Total volume of 6,539 posts indicates high information density, but one-sided consensus remains limited to a minority of names.
